frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Ambiguity aversion (rooted in the Ellsberg paradox, formalized by multiple-priors maxmin EU) means investors dislike situations where they cannot assign a single probability distribution; in finance it can explain limited stock-market participation, home bias / under-diversification, an ambiguity premium, and crisis amplification.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Ambiguity Aversion in Asset Pricing
